If any, no evidence or causal explanation for why one type or another may or may not be affected by lighting was provided. • Concern arises that the deterrence effect of lighting on crime might drive criminals to commit crimes in nearby areas, which is known as spatial displacement. Rather, it was found that there is diffusion of benefits to nearby areas, which means that improved street lighting as a crime-prevention measure has a beneficial influence beyond the targeted places. • Effects on crime are usually a minor aspect of street lighting that would influence residents’ satisfaction. Most did not believe that street lighting had a significant impact on crime levels. There were beliefs that crime had deeper causes and would happen anyway, even in daylight, or that lighting actually helps criminals. 29 • However, there was considerably more support for the premise that street lighting can have a role in reducing fear of crime than for the idea that street lighting can affect the occurrence of crime itself. • Evidence suggests that changes to mobility overall and travel mode choice in areas affected by reduced street lighting are likely to be minimal. One potential reason is that the impact may not be as direct as how crime and crash affect travel mode choice. But, given the correlation between street lighting and safety and security, street lighting may still play an important role in this, as also evidenced by the association between street lighting and physical activity such as walking and cycling. • The impact of light on human health and ecological systems has been a significant field of investigation in recent years. Health and ecology benefits from reduced light pollution have been noted. • One of the most attractive attributes of new lighting technology, such as LEDs and adaptive lighting, is the potential to reduce costs typically associated with energy consumption and maintenance. • While the new adaptive lighting technology offers a wide range of potential benefits (mainly in terms of energy savings), the safety and security impact of this technology on road users is yet to be evaluated due to the slow implementation of these systems in street and residential areas and the lack of supporting data. 2.4 Gaps in Existing Body of Work Based on the review of the existing literature, the following gaps have been identified: • While the new street lighting technology offers a wide range of potential benefits (mainly in terms of energy savings), it is necessary to evaluate the safety and security impact of this technology on road users, especially pedestrians.
